how: The starter combines already placing a logo with asking others to enlarge it.
Calls recruit helpers to enlarge the logo and later to add further drawings.
A call for another YES receives a bare offer to help in its reply branch.

statement: explaining canvas mechanics and local references while work is underway
how: Explanations make pixel placement mechanics and the local YES reference intelligible after building has begun.
Few helpers make even two unwanted pixels consequential, while larger lettering requires broader agreement.
Members negotiate backgrounds, borders, additions, lettering, and incompatible priorities for the shared drawing.
Builders report completed letters, remaining tidying, and progress after correcting the working location.
A request to locate the corner for protection receives its canvas coordinates.
A builder's placement report exposes an incorrect anchor and elicits corrected coordinates from the starter.
Reporting existing completed work cancels a duplicate proposal before it recruits a redundant build.
Members use placement scripts to retain chosen forms and solicit script use when the logo fails.
Automated preservation of an intentionally unfinished letter also rejects attempted helpful completion.
Parallel thread and chat routes require an explicit coordination process while leaving internal chat authority unresolved.
A visitor seeking a route for explaining a proposal is directed to the project thread and IRC team.
One room cannot test a population frequency, and a neighbour's reported Discord vote cannot establish this room's own government.
Members promise repairs, recruit automated upkeep, and maintain some pieces while drawing others.
A would-be defender first needs the drawing located, and another participant supplies its coordinates.
A reply identifies intended helpful completion as contrary to the official design rather than treating all altered pixels as outside vandalism.

Participants decline damaging expansion, propose a respectful redesign, and report a neighbour sanction against a would-be rocket remover.
Participants prevent possible conflict by rejecting a background that would overwrite other drawings without invoking a settled treaty.
Neighbours exchange explicit plan proposals, detailed pixel boundaries, and acceptance, while a truce request receives a redesign response.
A visitor carries a neighbouring room's plan and asks where to explain it to the project team.
A threatened neighbour receives manual help offers, script development, and reported placement, followed by thanks.
Paired scripts prioritize each room's own logo and allocate spare placement capacity to the other room's drawing.
Different explanations of Swedish tolerance do not establish the host's rules, approval process, or continuing authority over the drawing.
Reciprocal maintenance scripts establish a limited two-room cooperative arrangement without establishing a wider council or binding every placer.
Coded agreements receive acceptance and redesign proposals, leaving disputes over who may bind placers unobserved in the unavailable chats.
The inherited YES refrain becomes a canvas drawing target and continues through successive calls for more YESes.
The coded attack and defence calls name opponents without establishing a quarrel inherited from before the canvas.
Shared honour motivates helping, while the attack calls do not name inherited lore or ties as their reason for choosing rivals.
A mock-serious post explicitly identifies itself as an April Fools attempt alongside the drawing work.
Attribute April Fools keying only where supported, distinguishing the inherited YES chain from explicit prank claims and canvas automation.
A requester voluntarily cancels a duplicate proposal after discovering existing art, without establishing a host moderation rule for canvas posts.
Participants thank builders, announce completed YESes, and celebrate an inventory of finished drawings.
An end-of-event inventory records the reported outcome, while an explicit shutdown announcement receives a sad reply.
The coded record marks the ending and reports outcomes without establishing a dispute over cleaned copies or retained versions of history.
After shutdown, one participant recruits help to recreate the logo on a successor canvas and later congratulates the work.
Continuation on a successor canvas includes a fresh call and renewed building before the same author reports a good job.
The broad neighbour theme includes explicit attack calls that require contention as well as negotiated-order placement.
The attack branch supplies an aggressive call and shutdown response without establishing a sustained contest of taunts or victory claims.
The initial enlargement call receives a builder's report of working on the logo.
The starter's placing and enlargement call appear together, linking the role to recruitment without resolving separate onset times.
Reports of completed letters turn toward tidying, while later maintenance runs concurrently with drawing another piece.
Concern about overlapping drawings locally connects keeping work intact to neighbour discussion and a respectful redesign proposal.
A truce request receives an explicit promise of redesign for coexistence, supporting proposed restraint without proving its implementation.
A participant explicitly responds to the failing logo by calling for an extension and placement script.
A call to make another YES is answered by reporting completion before a third YES is started.
Celebration and outcome recording share one inventory, while later shutdown talk supplies no explicit celebration-caused preservation mechanism.
A successor effort follows shutdown talk in another thread, but its author does not link rebuilding to the earlier record or mourning.
Thin participation and a fight-or-abandon question do not establish that the room stopped fighting and relocated.
Shared visual instructions do not establish design settlement when participants still dispute colours or misread an intentional gap as unfinished work.
A posted call receives a bare help offer, establishing the local pair without testing the general account of refusals or silent acceptances.
A neighbour's damaged logo prompts a help request that receives offers of spare manual tiles and script assistance.
Distinguish the threatened requester's shortage from a donor offering spare manual tiles or lower-priority automated capacity.
The recorded aid follows a damage request and shared-capacity proposal rather than an explicit bargain exchanging help for space.
Recruitment and a late attack call both occur, but different threads and speakers leave the proposed causal transfer of recruited hands unestablished.
The Blue Corner attack branch records no direct refusal or apology, while restraint elsewhere does not establish an answer to that call.
One response to reported encroachment offers fighting back and calm negotiation as alternatives within the same turn.
The attack call has no coded continuation into taunts, victory claims, or a sustained contest with its named target.
A threatened neighbour's help request elicits reciprocal maintenance scripts, supporting cooperation at the model's smallest two-room range.
A duplicate call's voluntary removal establishes correction of redundant work rather than a flood-induced host posting boundary.
Agreement and invitations to discuss redesign do not supply the tentative arrow's required dispute over who can commit placers.
